rulebook.h1: Three cards, two teams, twelve points.
rulebook.lead: Each hand has up to three rounds and the strongest card takes each one. Two rounds take the hand. The game ends when a team reaches 12.
rulebook.variant.paulista: In paulista the manilha changes every hand.
rulebook.variant.mineiro: In mineiro the four manilhas are always the same.
rulebook.order.p: From strongest to weakest. The deck has no 8, 9 or 10. Outside the manilhas the suit does not count, so two kings tie.
rulebook.order.list: Order of the plain cards, from strongest to weakest
rulebook.order.note.paulista: Above them all sit the {manilhas}, which change every hand.
rulebook.order.note.mineiro: Above them all sit the four fixed {manilhas}.
rulebook.duel.tie: A tie: outside the manilhas the suit does not count.
rulebook.m.p: After the deal, one card from the deck is turned face up. The next rank in the order becomes manilha and beats everything. Pick a vira.
rulebook.m.wrap: After the 3, the order starts again.
rulebook.m.suits: Among the four, the suit decides.
rulebook.m.neworder: In this hand, the order becomes:
rulebook.m.say: Vira {vira}. The manilhas are {pl}: zap, copas, espadilha and pica-fumo, in that order.
rulebook.m.list: The four manilhas, from strongest to weakest
rulebook.m.p.mineiro: Mineiro has no vira. The four manilhas are always the same and beat every other card.
rulebook.m.plain.mineiro: The other fours, sevens and aces are plain cards.
rulebook.rounds.h: Rounds and who takes the hand
rulebook.rounds.p: Two rounds take the hand. Ties follow the cases below. After a tie, the player who opened the tied round opens the next one.
rulebook.rounds.caption: The five cases, from one team's point of view
rulebook.rounds.case.two: Two rounds won take the hand.
rulebook.rounds.case.firstTie: First round tied: the second decides.
rulebook.rounds.case.laterTie: Second or third round tied: the winner of the first takes it.
rulebook.rounds.case.twoTies: First and second tied: the third decides.
rulebook.t.p: {truco} is a bet: you say your team will win, and the hand becomes worth more.
rulebook.t.s1p: Before playing your card, tap Truco or press T. If the other team accepts, the hand goes from {from} to {to}.
rulebook.t.s2p: Accept: the hand becomes worth {to}. Running gives {run} to the caller. Calling {next} raises again, and now the first caller must answer.
rulebook.t.s3h: Take the hand, take it all
rulebook.t.s3p: Two rounds won take the hand and the points at stake. The ladder goes to 12: {ladder}. Teams take turns to raise and nobody skips a step.
rulebook.demo.start: The hand is worth {value}. Call truco to see the answers.
rulebook.demo.called: You called truco. If they accept, the hand is worth {value}. Now they answer.
rulebook.demo.raise.us: You called {call}. If they accept, the hand is worth {value}. Now they answer.
rulebook.demo.raise.them: They called {call}. If you accept, the hand is worth {value}. Now you answer.
rulebook.demo.accept.them: They accepted: the hand is worth {value}.
rulebook.demo.accept.us: You accepted: the hand is worth {value}.
rulebook.demo.top: Twelve is the top of the ladder: now you can only accept or run.
rulebook.onze.h.paulista: Mão de onze and mão de ferro
rulebook.onze.h.mineiro: Mão de dez and mão de ferro
rulebook.onze.p: When only one team reaches {n}, it decides before the first card: play for {value}, or run and the other team takes {run}. In 2 against 2, both players see each other's cards. Nobody calls truco in that hand.
rulebook.ferro.p: If both teams reach {n}, it is the mão de ferro: nobody sees their own cards and nobody calls truco. The hand decides the game.
rulebook.cover.p: You may play a card face down. It is worth nothing and the others do not see which card it was. It is not allowed in the first round or in the mão de ferro. On the keyboard, E turns it on and off.
rulebook.cover.caption: A face-down card loses to any card played face up.
rulebook.signals.p: Each player may send one signal per hand to the partner, before playing their first card. There are six: zap, copas, espadilha, pica-fumo, three and nothing. The partner always sees it, and each opponent sees it with a 25% chance. A signal may be a lie, and there are no signals in the mão de ferro.
rulebook.time.p: Each move has 30 seconds. When time runs out, the move is made for you and stays out of the human data. In rooms with friends the AI makes that move, and three timeouts in a row leave the seat to the AI until you come back.
rulebook.time.rooms: In rooms with friends: 15, 30 or 60 seconds, or no limit when every seat has a person.
rulebook.match.p: The match goes to 12 {tentos}. With the best of three house rule, each game to 12 is a {queda} and the score goes back to 0. The first team to win two quedas wins.
rulebook.house.p: Whoever creates a room with friends can turn these options on. Matches against the AI use the rules above.
rulebook.house.raiseAnyTime: Call truco at any moment of the hand, also out of turn.
rulebook.house.faceDown: Face-down cards from the first round, except for the player who leads the hand.
rulebook.house.allTie: Three tied rounds: the hand goes to the team of the player who led it.
rulebook.house.iron: The mão de ferro played as a normal hand.
rulebook.house.ladder8: In mineiro, the ladder with eight: 2, 4, 8, 10 and 12.
rulebook.house.signals: Signals: only the partner sees them, each opponent sees them with a 25% chance, or everyone sees them.
rulebook.house.time: Time per move: 15, 30 or 60 seconds, or no limit when every seat has a person.
rulebook.keys.p: At the table you can play without a mouse and without touching the screen.
rulebook.keys.cards: play the first, second or third card, from left to right
rulebook.keys.t: calls truco or raises the call
rulebook.keys.a: accepts the call or plays the mão de onze
rulebook.keys.e: turns the face-down card on and off
rulebook.keys.esc: closes the menu, the dialog or the open list
rulebook.keys.arrows: move between your cards; Enter or Space plays the card
rulebook.sources.p: The default rules come from tournament regulations and popular online rooms. What changes from house to house became a room option.
rulebook.src.uffs: Truco paulista regulations, Universidade Federal da Fronteira Sul, 2024 (Portuguese)
rulebook.src.banc: Truco tournament regulations, São Paulo Bank Workers' Union, 2017 (Portuguese)
rulebook.dialog.title: Quick rules
rulebook.dialog.manilhas.lead: Vira: {card}. The next rank, {rank}, becomes manilha and beats every other card. Among them, the suit decides:
rulebook.dialog.manilhas.generalLead: The rank after the vira becomes manilha and beats every other card. Among the four, the suit decides:
rulebook.dialog.manilhas.fixedLead: Mineiro has no vira. The manilhas are always these, from strongest to weakest:
rulebook.dialog.step1p: If the other team accepts, the hand goes from {from} to {to}.
rulebook.dialog.step2p: Accept, run (the caller takes {run}) or call {next}.
rulebook.dialog.step3p: After truco come {ladder}, with the teams taking turns.
rulebook.dialog.keys: Keys: 1, 2 and 3 play the cards. T calls truco, A accepts, C runs, E covers the next card, R opens these rules.
